question: Should exact matched requester consumption count as durable descendant delivery proof even when the final outward cron delivery later fails?
rationale: The code is internally coherent, but this is a delivery-contract choice that changes retry/finalization semantics and stored restore behavior beyond what unit tests can authorize.

options.title: Require proof and accept narrow requester-consumption credit
options.body: Ask for redacted live cron/background or SQLite restore proof, then accept the intentionally narrow consumed-run boundary if maintainers agree it is the right delivery contract.

options.title: Require outward delivery before descendant credit
options.body: Keep descendant rows pending/retryable unless the requester result is durably delivered outward, which preserves stricter visible-delivery semantics at the cost of the PR's stated failure-mode fix.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox/spool work
options.body: Pause this PR and solve the requester-consumed case inside the broader durable completion inbox design tracked by related subagent delivery issues.

recommendation.title: Require proof and accept narrow requester-consumption credit
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted live cron/background or SQLite restore proof, then accept the intentionally narrow consumed-run boundary if maintainers agree it is the right delivery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans subagent delivery state and SQLite restore compatibility, where steipete has recent adjacent history and broad agent-runtime ownership signals.
